title: Brahmandapurana, book 1
source: sa_brahmANDapurANa.txt; GRETIL (gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (data entry: members of the Sansknet Project)
reply:
These verses describe time (kāla), the year-cycle and its presiding deities. I found only a few that state something close to kinship, and none that clearly name a person as a son, daughter, wife or successor.

Candidates I checked and rejected:
- 1,13.124: "brahmaputraḥ prajāpatiḥ" calls the sun-year a son of Brahmā, but the verse names no personal subject for the relation. The subject is Bhāskara as a personified year, not a named person. I left it out.
- 1,13.125 and 1,13.127: "pitāmahaḥ" and "prapitāmahaḥ" are epithets, not statements about named individuals.
- 1,13.119 and 1,13.136: Rudra is said to be born from Brahmā ("ahaṅkārādudagrudraḥ saṃbhūto brahmaṇāstu yaḥ"; "brahmāṇo vaktrādudansamabhavad bhavaḥ"). This is a birth from Brahmā, and the verse gives Rudra and Bhava as the same figure. Rudra is named, so it could count as son_of Brahmā, but the text does not say "son". In 1,13.119 the origin is from ahaṅkāra, and Brahmā is the agent ("saṃbhūto brahmaṇā"). Because the filiation is not stated in words, I excluded both.
- 1,13.145: the metres Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī are called "yonayaḥ" of Vanaspati, which is not a kinship between persons.
- 1,13.148–149: "ṛtuputrārttavāḥ pañca" mentions sons of the seasons, but names no individuals.

Nothing qualifies, so I return no statements.
